## Decision 1: the map is generated by a Python script, not edited in Tiled

`tools/level/phase1.py` turns an ASCII layout into `src/assets/tilemaps/phase1.json`.
The script is the source of truth; the JSON is the build input. It keeps the map
diffable, needs no Tiled install, and lets the script print a validation report (hole
widths, run-up lengths, tallest obstacle, ceiling height) that stands in for a playtest
while browser runs need the owner's authorization. Alternative rejected: hand-editing
the JSON, which no reviewer can read.

## Decision 2: the tileset is assembled at runtime from the wall artwork

`brick_wall.png` and `wooden_wall.png` are single outlined blocks, not tilesets. Every
scenery PNG shares one geometry: transparent padding of 4 authored px times its upscale
factor, and a 1 authored px outline. `PhaseTileset` slices each block into four variants
— middle (no outline), top (outline on top), left and right corners (outline on top and
one side) — into a 512×64 canvas texture, and the map binds to it by key through
`addTilesetImage('tiles', 'tiles_phase1')`. The map JSON names an image file that never
exists on disk, which is fine because the texture is already in the cache.
Alternative rejected: shipping a hand-cut tileset PNG, which blocks code on art.

## Decision 3: authored placement, seeded decoration

Everything the player collides with is authored in the map: ground, holes, obstacles and
coins. Decoration has no gameplay meaning, so it is scattered at runtime by
`Phaser.Math.RandomDataGenerator` seeded with a per-phase string from `PhaseConfig`. The
seed makes every guest see the same phase while keeping hundreds of props out of the map
file. Alternative rejected: authoring decoration too, which triples the map's size for
no gameplay gain.

## Decision 4: hurting obstacles overlap, they do not collide

A cactus that is solid and hurts would, with no i-frames and no knockback, drain hearts
while the player is pressed against it. So hazards have no solid body: they overlap, and
a heart is spent only when the overlap starts, guarded by `damageCooldownMs`. Blocking
obstacles are static bodies with no damage. The classification lives in
`gameplay-scenery-obstacles.md`.

## Decision 5: one debug flag

`gameConfig.debug.enabled` gates the rectangle textures, the player's texture choice,
the overlay and nothing else, each with an early return. `import.meta.env.DEV` is
rejected: this is a content toggle the owner sets, not a build concern, and one config
value stays greppable when Muri's art replaces the rectangle.

## Decision 6: `PhaseScene` is a base class, not a scene

It is never registered in `main.ts`, so the scene count stays at ten. Phase 1 to 3 are
subclasses that pass a key and a `PhaseConfig`. Any branch on the scene key is a defect.
